subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: A plagal cadence consists of which progression?
questions.explain: The plagal ('Amen') cadence moves from the subdominant (IV) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: A pivot chord in modulation is best defined as which of the following?
options: A chromatic chord with no diatonic function
The final chord of a phrase only
A chord borrowed from the parallel major
A chord common to both the old and new keys used to effect the change
questions.explain: A pivot chord belongs diatonically to both keys, smoothing the transition during a modulation.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: In a Classical concerto first movement, the cadenza traditionally occurs at which point?
options: At the very opening before the orchestra plays
In the middle of the development only
Near the end, over a tonic six-four before the final tutti
questions.explain: The cadenza, a virtuosic solo passage, typically falls near the movement's end on a cadential six-four leading to the closing tutti.

questions.q: A 'reel', another Celtic dance type, is usually in...?
options: Simple quadruple time (4/4 or cut common) with a flowing quaver movement
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple quadruple time with continuous even quavers.

questions.q: Swing-era big bands such as Count Basie's typically organised their players into which sectional layout?
questions.explain: Big bands are built around a saxophone section, a brass section and a rhythm section.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
A return to strict ragtime forms
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: Early rock 'n' roll of the 1950s (e.g. Chuck Berry) frequently combined the twelve-bar blues with which other key ingredient?
questions.explain: Rock 'n' roll fused the twelve-bar blues with a strong backbeat on beats 2 and 4.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: In music technology, 'sampling' is best described as...?
options: Taking a portion of an existing sound recording and reusing it within a new piece
Recording in a single continuous take
questions.explain: Sampling reuses a fragment of an existing recording as material within a new track.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: The compositional device of 'augmentation' refers to...?
options: Lengthening the note values of a theme, usually doubling them
Raising the pitch of a theme
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens a theme's note values, typically doubling each duration.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.

questions.q: A circle-of-fifths progression characteristically moves the bass by which interval?
questions.explain: A circle-of-fifths sequence moves root by root down a fifth (equivalently up a fourth) each step.

questions.q: Neoclassicism in the 20th century is characterised by which approach?
options: Reviving Classical and Baroque forms with modern harmony
questions.explain: Neoclassicism, associated with Stravinsky, revisits older forms and clarity while applying a modern harmonic language.

questions.q: An interrupted cadence most commonly progresses from which chord to which?
questions.explain: An interrupted (deceptive) cadence moves from V to vi, thwarting the expected resolution to the tonic.

questions.q: Wagner's term for a recurring musical theme associated with a character or idea is which?
questions.explain: Wagner used leitmotifs, short recurring themes representing characters, objects or ideas in his music dramas.

questions.q: When 'arranging' an existing melody for a new ensemble, a composer is chiefly concerned with...?
options: Transposing it down exactly one semitone only
Inventing an entirely new melody unrelated to the original
Re-scoring and adapting existing material for different forces while retaining its essence
questions.explain: Arranging adapts and re-scores existing material for different forces while preserving its identity.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
Free improvisation with no fixed form
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: In the alap–jhor–jhalla–gat structure, the 'gat' section is distinguished by...?
options: A return to the unmetred opening
A solo drone with no melody
The entry of the tabla and a fixed, composed melody with a regular tala
questions.explain: The gat is the composed, metred section where the tabla enters and a fixed melody is set within a tala.

questions.q: Schubert is especially celebrated for his contribution to which genre?
questions.explain: Schubert composed over 600 Lieder, defining the Romantic art song.

questions.q: An appoggiatura is best defined as which?
options: A dissonant note approached by leap and resolved by step
A note approached and left by step
questions.explain: An appoggiatura is an accented non-harmony note usually approached by leap and resolved by step.

questions.q: In Celtic folk music, a 'jig' is most commonly in which metre?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance typically in compound 6/8 time.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: The music has no fixed pulse
A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: A 'cyclic' or 'ostinato' pattern, common in African drumming, is...?
options: A short rhythmic or melodic pattern repeated continuously as a foundation
A pattern that constantly changes and never repeats
questions.explain: Cyclic patterns repeat a short rhythmic or melodic cell continuously, forming the music's foundation.
